newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its policy-making council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent.
Economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday had said that the chances of the Bundesbank cutting leading German interest rates at today's meeting, or at any other time in 1997, were slim.

Ten economists polled by Reuters said they did not expect the Bundesbank to cut its leading interest rates this week. Nine did not expect a further cut in the discount and Lombard rates this year to help stimulate the economy during the year.

Any lingering expectations of a rate cut this week were further dampened on Tuesday by comments by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, quoted in a newspaper interview as saying he saw no need for a cut in German rates for the time being.
The Bundesbank last cut its discount and Lombard rates in April last year. It cut the repo to three percent in August.
